title: Human-centred safety gating rotations and handoff protocols (WIP)
body:
Purpose:
This is a working sketch for a human-centred approach to safety gating, steward rotations, and handoff protocols for progressive exposures (micro-exposures / staggered slices / interleaved A/B). The goal: create predictable human workflows that reduce cognitive load on on-call and product stewards while preserving fast iteration velocity.

Background / motivation:
- We keep shipping smaller LLM changes and experiment surfaces that can produce rare but high-impact harms (confident hallucinations, unsafe outputs, policy hits).
- Automation covers many failure modes but humans are still needed for contextual judgment and stakeholder comms.
- Current handoff rituals are ad-hoc, unclear who owns the decision during the first 24–72 hours of a micro-exposure. That increases time-to-revert and inconsistent communication.

High-level proposal (summary):
1) A short steward rotation for each progressive activation: 4 roles for the first 72h window: steward, observer, SRE-oncall, comms lead.  
2) A compact preflight checklist (synthetic smoke, telemetry baselines, kill-switch validation).  
3) A simple signal contract (primary, secondary, and soft signals) and an escalation ladder with timeboxes.  
4) Lightweight handoff artifacts (one-pager + short Slack template + rollback command).

Roles & responsibilities (first 72h):
- Steward (product/owner): overall decision authority for the experiment; responsible for hypothesis, guardrail thresholds, and escalation decisions. Idle window: 9am–5pm local overlap preferred.
- Observer (engineer on the feature): maintains the experiment instrumentation dashboard and runs quick triage; owns immediate triage steps and notes.
- SRE-oncall: validates system-level metrics (latency, infra errors, resource saturation) and executes rollback if system stability breach occurs.
- Comms lead (solutions/CS or comms PM): drafts public-facing status updates and coordinates customer outreach if needed.

Rotation plan (how to staff):
- Day-zero (activation): steward + observer + SRE + comms assigned and paged in a short kickoff (10–15 min).  
- Days 0–1: steward and observer shadow closely (hourly check-ins optional).  
- Days 1–3: rotation moves to 8-hour checkpoints; steward remains the decision owner but can hand authority to a designated deputy for nights/holidays.  
- Longer exposures: transition to weekly steward cadence and become a normal PM-owned feature with regular oncall integration.

Preflight checklist (must pass before exposure):
- Synthetic smoke traffic simulating top-20 prompt shapes ran for 30m with no safety flags or >95th percentile latencies.  
- Regression tests: canonical prompt set evaluated against baseline model; no more than X% drop in expected quality metrics (define per feature).
- Kill-switch test: verified rollback command successfully disables route and restores traffic to fallback variant within SLA window.
- Observability: telemetry dashboards (listed below) are live, alerting hooks active, and pager routing confirmed.
- Stakeholders: legal/safety notified if the experiment touches PII, PHI, or regulated categories.

Signal taxonomy (short):
- Primary signals (actionable within 5–15m): safety flag counts (policy triggers), customer-reported TOS violations, surge in ‘user report’ submissions, automated toxicity scores above threshold.  
- Secondary signals (contextual): semantic quality deltas from eval harness, reranker mismatch rates, increased low-confidence outputs.
- System signals (SRE): 99th percentile latency spikes, error budget burn, model OOMs, infra throttles.
- Soft signals: subjective user experience metrics (NPS snippets, CS feedback), small sample human review failures.

Dashboards & telemetry minimal set: (each tile should be visible in the steward dashboard)
- Safety flag trend (1h / 6h / 24h) and per-slice breakdown.  
- Hallucination proxy: contradiction count vs knowledge baseline (synthetic eval).
- Quality delta: score vs baseline on canonical prompt set.
- Latency P95/P99 and error rate.
- Cost-per-response trend for the experiment slice.
- Customer reports / escalations stream.

Escalation ladder (timeboxed):
- Soft deviation: if any primary safety signal > threshold for 15m, steward gets notified and observer triages within 30m.
- Hard deviation: if primary safety signal > hard threshold for 5m OR system signal severe, SRE executes immediate rollback (no steward permission needed for system breaches).
- Comms: for any revert/partial revert, comms lead drafts a short update within 60 minutes and posts to the designated channel and status page.

Handoff artifacts (templates):
- One-line experiment summary (template):  
  - "Experiment: {name} — variant {A/B} — slices {user_cohort} — steward {name} — rollout start {datetime} — kill-switch {command}"
- Slack kickoff template (used at activation):  
  - "[EXPERIMENT START] {name} | steward: @{steward} | observer: @{observer} | SRE: @{sre} | comms: @{comms}. Kill-switch: `{rollback_command}`. Dashboards: {link}. Watchlist: safety flags, latency P99. Checking in at +1h, +6h, +24h unless escalated"
- Rollback command (example):  
  - `redwood rollout disable --route=experiment-123 --reason="auto-rollback-safety" --force`  
  (documented in runbook and accessible to SRE-oncall and steward).

Incident quick-play (if safety flag surge):
1) Observer: confirm raw outputs and attach 3 example transcripts to the incident ticket.
2) Steward: review whether issue is model-behavior (policy/hallucination) or prompt/feature mis-shape. If model-behavior likely, escalate to Research/Applied-ML.
3) SRE: if system metrics abnormal, run rollback immediately; inform steward.
4) Comms: prepare internal blurb and public template if customer-facing.
5) Postmortem: short 24h blameless note with actions and whether sandboxed tests could have caught the issue.

Low-friction practices to reduce friction: 
- Keep steward artifact to a single page with direct links to 3 dashboards and the rollback command.
- Default steward timeout: if no steward response within 45m and signal is degrading, the observer escalates to SRE for conservative revert.
- Pre-authorized SRE rollback for system breaches (explicit allowed scope).

Open questions / tradeoffs (needs alignment):
- What numerical thresholds for safety flags are reasonable? (ops currently uses absolute counts; need normalized per-slice rate).
- Night coverage: do we require 24/7 steward coverage for any exposure >24h? (cost vs risk tradeoff)
- How to integrate human-review sampling without blocking throughput (sampled cold-path + async annotation?).

Operational checklist (short actionable steps before activation):
- [ ] Fill one-pager and pin to experiment card.
- [ ] Run synthetic smoke for 30m and save results.
- [ ] Confirm rollback command and permissions with SRE.
- [ ] Create Slack kickoff message and schedule check-ins.

Next steps / owners:
- Ravi: draft a short telemetry normalization doc (due 2025-11-20).
- Sofia: prototype the steward dashboard with the minimal tiles (due 2025-12-05).
- Marco: add rollback command to infra runbook and validate permissioning (due 2025-11-15).
- Ava: socialize this sketch in next crossfunc rollout sync and collect feedback (due 2025-11-13).

Notes to self / rough thoughts:
- Want to keep human burden minimal; stewards should rarely be asked for minute-by-minute triage.
- Consider a small "standby" budget (rotation credit) for stewards so teams roster coverage fairly.
- Could we add a tiny ML classifier that flags likely hallucination bursts and surfaces representative transcripts to the steward? Low payoff but might speed decisions.

References / links (internal):
- rollout signal lexicon (confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/ROLL-314
- current synthetic harness ticket: JIRA-5821
- shepherding script PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/rollout-scripts/pull/142

If you read this and have immediate suggestions: add inline comments or drop short notes in #rollout-stewards.

-- Ava
